notes: SHARED QUESTION L (rows 1985-GR-VIII.4.4.4-7, 1985-GR-XIII.4.5.4-5, 1985-GR-XIII.4.5.4-11): which label convention do the OPEN label steps follow? ANSWER: the implementor's (§1985 Implementor-Defined Element List items 57, 58, 60, 61; VII.3.6.3 GR2). ISO 2023 does not control: LABEL RECORDS was deleted in 2002. The convention IS NOW RECORDED, which the refuters did not see: docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.7 (kb/Work PB5070, present in the probed tree) says 'WiseOwl COBOL claims no label processing, so LABEL RECORDS and VALUE OF are null facilities in function' and 'no label is read or written'. Under that convention a host file carries no label records. OMITTED and an omitted clause therefore do nothing at OPEN, and a STANDARD file is in the GR's 'specified but not present' case, whose behaviour 'is undefined', so any behaviour conforms. GnuCOBOL (next in precedence) also accepts LABEL RECORDS and processes no labels. That is recalled, not measured: this host has no GnuCOBOL. One gap remains in the documentation, not in the behaviour: section 3.7 does not cite the OPEN/CLOSE label rules or items 57, 58, 60 and 61, so a reader cannot find the 'specified conventions' from the rules. Its entry should cite them. Applied here: steps a-c are null under the recorded convention, and step d (proceed as OUTPUT, positioned after the last record, GR10) holds. The second report is appended after the first.

next.reason: 1985: "When the EXTEND phrase is specified and the LABEL RECORDS clause indicates label records are present"; 2023: "GR-14.9.27.4-15 covers OPEN EXTEND positioning only; no LABEL RECORDS clause or label processing in any candidate". 2023 drops the LABEL RECORDS clause and label processing. The OPEN EXTEND rules give positioning only and nowhere state the label steps a-d.
